PullRequest.Title: POC: Chat session state frames
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #333253

## POC

Explores persistent state frames around chat editor sessions so multiple sessions expose actionable status without relying on focus.

## Feature flag

The entire feature is gated by the false-by-default experimental setting:

```json
"chat.experimental.sessionStateIndicator.enabled": true
```

When disabled, no state classes, frames, animations, or input-progress replacement are applied.

## Behavior when enabled

- Keeps visited idle sessions at the default chat editor appearance.
- Shows a light-gray one-stroke frame for completions not yet visited, clearing it when the session receives focus.
- Shows a pulsing green one-stroke frame while the agent is working.
- Shows an error-red frame and halo while a session needs input.
- Excludes inline chat, Quick Chat, and the Chat view pane beside the sessions list.
- Uses the outer running frame instead of the input progress border.
- Keeps state frames visible above the Prompt Timeline sticky header and rail.
- Honors reduced motion and high-contrast themes.

## Validation

- Targeted ESLint for the changed TypeScript files
- Targeted stylelint for `chat.css`
- `npm run compile-client`
- Pre-commit hygiene checks
- Live Code OSS validation with the feature flag both disabled and enabled
- Live validation across visited idle, unvisited completion, running, blocked, sticky-header, and multi-editor states

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed selector, full-widget dimensions, state call path, infinite lifetime, and per-frame paint mechanism are explicit in the code. Exact milliseconds vary by GPU, display scale, editor size, and number of split groups, which affects severity but not the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Per-frame paint and raster work for a full-height, up-to-950px-wide editor pseudo-element and its blurred shadow
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The non-composited box-shadow is interpolated every animation frame for the entire request duration; cost grows with editor area, display scale, request duration, and the number of simultaneously visible running chat editors in split groups.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Sustained paint/raster load, increased CPU/GPU usage, and dropped frames while an agent is working
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this change there was no whole-editor state pseudo-element. In-progress feedback, when enabled, was confined to the much smaller chat input border; the changed TypeScript also disables that input indicator when the new session indicator is enabled.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The added keyframes interpolate the shadow blur/color, and the added in-progress rule runs them infinitely on an absolutely positioned pseudo-element inset over the entire `.interactive-session`, which is `height: 100%` and can be 950px wide.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT lines 29-37 add box-shadow interpolation between two values, and RIGHT line 60 applies it as an infinite 1.4s animation to the new full-session pseudo-element. RIGHT `chatWidget.ts:977` disables the prior input-only indicator when this feature is active, making this newly added broad animation the replacement.
Findings.Title: Avoid animating box-shadow across the full chat editor
Findings.Impact: With `chat.experimental.sessionStateIndicator.enabled` enabled, every visible running chat editor continuously repaints a full-editor shadow. Long agent runs or multiple running sessions in split editor groups can consume rendering capacity and make scrolling, typing, and other workbench animations jank.
Findings.Evidence: `.interactive-session` is defined at `chat.css:6-12` as `height: 100%`, `max-width: 950px`, and positioned; the new pseudo-element uses `inset: 0` at lines 42-44. `chatWidget.ts:1003-1018` maps `requestInProgress` to `chat-state-in-progress`, while lines 2774-2782 subscribe to accumulated view-model changes for streamed responses. CSS `box-shadow` interpolation is paint/raster work rather than a compositor-only opacity/transform update, so it repeats at display frame cadence independently of model-event batching.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep the shadow geometry static and pulse only compositor-friendly opacity, for example with two pre-styled pseudo-elements or a nested layer whose opacity is animated; avoid interpolating `box-shadow` itself across the full editor.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run one or more agent requests in visible chat editor splits with the experimental indicator enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Submitting a request starts the existing agent invocation; model progress reaches ChatViewModel and the accumulated widget listener sets `chat-state-in-progress`. Browser frame production then continuously paints the new pseudo-element until the request leaves the active state. The animation is directly on the rendering critical path, while the agent invocation runs asynchronously.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke the existing chat agent and stream progress back to the model
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One top-level invocation per submitted request; provider-specific tool or subagent calls are pre-existing and not caused by this diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same agent invocation occurred before the diff. In-progress feedback was absent at whole-editor scope and, when configured, confined to the smaller input border.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The request awaits the agent invocation, while the new animation runs concurrently for that pending lifetime. The diff adds no await or extra boundary call.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One full-height pseudo-element per visible running chat editor; realistic cardinality is one in a single group or two to four across split editor groups. Paint repeats at display-frame cadence for the full request duration and scales with editor area and device scale.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each visible running editor owns an independent infinite CSS animation. Model events are debounced with delay 0 before the class update, but CSS frame work is neither batched nor coalesced across editors.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The setting read is synchronous in-memory configuration state. There is no raster-result cache that can eliminate frames because box-shadow blur/color are interpolated each frame; warm model/configuration state does not change the animation cost.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added keyframes interpolate box-shadow, the added rule is infinite, the target is inset over a height-100%, up-to-950px-wide widget, and the TypeScript maps requestInProgress to the selector.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact paint time depends on GPU/software rendering, display scale, editor dimensions, and split count. The full-editor non-composited property animation and request-lifetime repetition are certain; those environment factors make the severity medium rather than high.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable repeated rendering work: the new full-editor box-shadow interpolation creates sustained paint/raster load and can drop frames during long or concurrent agent runs.

Scenarios.Scenario: Stream responses with the feature disabled or in unsupported chat hosts
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each accumulated ChatViewModel change now calls `updateSessionStateIndicator`; it reads observable/config/focus state and applies forced class toggles, then the pre-existing list update path continues. No subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network boundary is invoked by the added indicator call after tracing it.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Calls scale with accumulated response-change batches and live widgets; unsupported hosts short-circuit the configuration read, and all indicator classes remain false.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous on the renderer event loop, one invocation per accumulated event batch per affected widget. DOMTokenList forced toggles do not rewrite classes when the requested false state already matches.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Configuration state and observables are in memory; there is no cold I/O. Event.accumulate coalesces synchronous response changes with a zero-delay debounce.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that the work is unconditional, but also high that it is bounded and substantially smaller than existing work on the same event.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very high-rate providers may produce many batches, but the incremental work is several in-memory reads and no-op class checks beside an existing list/content update path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: the disabled-path overhead is real but lacks evidence of a concrete user-visible regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Complete an unfocused editor session and later focus it
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The final model event transitions the local state from active to idle and adds the unvisited class; a captured focus event later calls the updater once to clear it. The browser applies a static border/short transition. No expensive external boundary is reached by the changed completion or focus handlers.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One completion transition and at most one clearing update per session completion, multiplied by the number of open chat editors.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Completion updates can occur independently in split editors; each is a bounded class-state transition rather than recurring work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Unvisited state is two booleans retained on each widget and reset on view-model replacement; no cache keys or negative cache behavior exist.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from the state helper, model listener, focus tracker, and view-model reset path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; cardinality is bounded by completions and focus visits.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance finding: retained state is constant-size and the focus tracker is registered with widget disposal.

Scenarios.Scenario: Toggle the experimental setting while chat widgets are open
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The configuration service broadcasts one event; each live widget updates the old input border state and new session classes synchronously. No subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network boundary is reached.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Two bounded updater calls per live widget for a user-initiated setting change; live widget count is normally small.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Configuration listeners execute synchronously per widget on the renderer event loop; there is no asynchronous fan-out or burst of boundary calls.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The new boolean is served from configuration memory. Enabling starts the CSS animation only for widgets whose current model is active; disabling removes the classes and stops it.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from the changed configuration listener and host gating.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Widget count can vary, but setting changes are rare and each handler is constant work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: setting-toggle fan-out is bounded and off the recurring interaction path.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all seven changed files. Reported one medium rendering regression: the opt-in in-progress state interpolates box-shadow every frame over a full chat editor. Checked the unconditional indicator updates and focus-tracker lifecycle; they are bounded, registered for disposal, and do not independently meet the reporting threshold. No regression-fix learning signal was present.
